newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA sees passenger growth in Asia, Central Asia.
newsitem.headline: IATA sees passenger growth in Asia, Central Asia.

text.p: The world airlines body IATA said it expected global international scheduled passenger traffic to grow an average 7.1 percent a year until 2000, led by Northeast and Southeast Asia as well as former Soviet Central Asia.

The International Air Transport Association, whose 250 member companies account for over 90 percent of world scheduled passenger traffic, also said in a statement on Tuesday that Northeast Asia would continue to grow by 9.2 percent a year.

IATA said in its latest passenger forecast, which included data from non-members as well, that it expected world international scheduled passenger numbers to reach 522 million in 2000 and nearly 800 million in 2010, up from almost 400 million now.
